PAT PAU - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


82-year-old woman with hypertension and hyperlipidemia admitted for new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.


Presented with cough, shortness of breath, wheezing, intermittent chest discomfort, lightheadedness, and dizziness.


Converted to sinus rhythm following rhythm control therapy with amiodarone and digoxin.


Initial cardiac evaluation showed no acute ischemic ECG changes, negative serial troponins, and no radiographic evidence of acute cardiopulmonary process.


Echocardiogram was ordered for further cardiac assessment.


Ongoing evaluation for whether atrial fibrillation was triggered by acute stress or possible viral respiratory illness versus representing a new persistent arrhythmia process.


SOAP Note
Subjective


Patient evaluated during inpatient cardiology follow-up.


Presented with symptoms beginning the day prior including shortness of breath, cough, wheezing, intermittent midsternal chest discomfort, lightheadedness, and dizziness.


Symptoms improved following rhythm control therapy.


Reports cough but denies fever, chills, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.


Long-term cardiac follow-up with Dr. Zeger discussed.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Alert, no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response documented during admission. Currently rhythm controlled following therapy.
Respiratory: Presented with cough, shortness of breath, and wheezing. Chest radiograph without acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
Neurologic: Lightheadedness and dizziness associated with presenting symptoms. No focal neurologic deficits documented.
Abdomen: No acute abdominal concerns documented.
Laboratory data reviewed. WBC 5.6 K/µL, hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, sodium 136 mmol/L, potassium 3.8 mmol/L, BUN 14 mg/dL, creatinine 1.01 mg/dL, BNP 128 pg/mL, troponin I 0.010 with repeat 0.013, TSH 0.716. COVID-19 testing negative.
ECG: Initial ECG showed sinus rhythm at 89 bpm without acute ischemic changes. Repeat ECG demonstrated atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate 132 bpm.
Assessment


New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (ICD-10: I48.91)


Shortness of breath (ICD-10: R06.02)


Acute chest pain (ICD-10: R07.9)


Dizziness and giddiness (ICD-10: R42)


Plan


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to new-onset atrial fibrillation requiring rhythm management, symptom evaluation, and determination of long-term arrhythmia strategy.


Continue rhythm monitoring on telemetry.


Continue amiodarone therapy as directed.


Further atrial fibrillation management to be guided by clinical course and cardiac evaluation.


Echocardiogram ordered for assessment of cardiac structure and function.


Continue evaluation for possible acute stress or viral respiratory trigger contributing to atrial fibrillation onset.


Continue follow-up with primary cardiologist Dr. Zeger as appropriate.


Monitor for recurrent symptomatic arrhythmia, chest discomfort, hypotension, or other clinical changes.


Nursing Communication


Continue telemetry monitoring.


Notify cardiology for recurrent symptomatic atrial fibrillation, tachycardia, hypotension, chest pain, worsening shortness of breath, or hemodynamic changes.


Monitor respiratory symptoms and clinical status.


Continue monitoring response to rhythm management.

Salient Cardiac Features


74-year-old man with severe multivessel coronary artery disease status post CABG x4 with left atrial appendage ligation on 08/25/2026.


Tachy-brady/junctional rhythm status post permanent pacemaker placement on 08/30/2026.


Pacemaker site healing well with dressing management and ongoing site surveillance.


Acute on chronic iron-deficiency anemia with ongoing concern for gastrointestinal blood loss and hemoglobin decline.


Recent EGD demonstrated gastric ulcers/small bleeding sites; further GI evaluation including possible capsule endoscopy or additional evaluation under consideration.


Volume overload with improving edema on diuretic therapy requiring monitoring of renal function and electrolytes.


Vein harvest site infection managed with antibiotic therapy.


SOAP Note
Subjective


Patient evaluated during inpatient cardiology follow-up.


Patient awaiting discharge once anemia and bleeding concerns are adequately addressed.


Recent endoscopy findings reviewed, with concern for ongoing gastrointestinal blood loss.


Further GI evaluation to be guided by clinical course and gastroenterology recommendations.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: No acute distress, awake and alert.
Cardiovascular: Status post CABG x4 and permanent pacemaker placement. Pacemaker site healing well with dressing in place.
Respiratory: No acute respiratory concerns documented.
Extremities: Improving lower-extremity edema with lower extremities wrapped. Scrotal swelling improving.
Laboratory data reviewed. Hemoglobin 7.4, WBC 5.0 K/µL, sodium 133 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, BUN 35 mg/dL, creatinine 1.32 mg/dL, BNP 457.
Assessment


Acute on chronic anemia with concern for ongoing gastrointestinal blood loss (ICD-10: D64.9)


Gastrointestinal bleeding with gastric ulcers (ICD-10: K92.2)


Coronary artery disease status post CABG x4 (ICD-10: I25.10, Z95.1)


Volume overload (ICD-10: E87.70)


Presence of cardiac pacemaker (ICD-10: Z95.0)


Superficial infection of vein harvest site (ICD-10: T81.41XA)


Plan


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to ongoing gastrointestinal blood loss with significant anemia, management of antithrombotic considerations following CABG, volume management, and postoperative cardiac care.


Continue close CBC monitoring and evaluate need for transfusion support based on hemoglobin trend and clinical status.


Continue IV proton pump inhibitor therapy.


Continue coordination with gastroenterology regarding ongoing bleeding evaluation and possible additional intervention.


Monitor volume status, intake/output, edema, renal function, and electrolytes during diuretic therapy.


Continue post-CABG cardiac therapy as clinically appropriate.


Continue pacemaker site surveillance and maintain clean dressing technique.


Continue wound care for vein harvest site infection.


Continue telemetry monitoring.


Continue PT/OT and mobilization as tolerated.


Nursing Communication


Monitor hemoglobin and signs of ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding.


Monitor pacemaker site for drainage, erythema, swelling, wound separation, or other signs of infection.


Continue vein harvest site wound surveillance.


Monitor intake/output, edema, renal function, and electrolytes during diuresis.


Notify cardiology for pacemaker-site changes, hemodynamic instability, significant arrhythmia, worsening volume overload, or other acute cardiac concerns.

WIL SEK - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


72-year-old man with history of kidney and liver transplantation, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, and recent hospitalization complicated by new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.


Currently in sinus rhythm on oral amiodarone.


Congestive heart failure/volume overload attributed to diastolic dysfunction/stiff heart physiology, requiring continued diuretic therapy.


Echocardiogram demonstrates LVEF 50%, normal RV systolic function, dilated IVC with estimated RAP 15 mmHg, and pulmonary artery pressure approximately 46 mmHg.


Anticoagulation with Eliquis planned as part of ongoing atrial fibrillation management.


Renal allograft function improved with creatinine approximately 1.25 after recent acute kidney injury.


Acute hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure has clinically improved.


SOAP Note
Subjective


Patient seen during cardiology follow-up.


Discussed ongoing cardiac medication management and need for continued outpatient follow-up.


Patient will require ongoing diuretic therapy after discharge for volume management.


Continued transplant follow-up through UCLA was encouraged, with local cardiology coordination as appropriate.


If patient elects to continue follow-up with this cardiology practice, close outpatient reassessment with physician or nurse practitioner within five working days after discharge was discussed.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Resting in bed, no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rhythm. Recent atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, currently controlled on oral amiodarone.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation anteriorly and laterally. Oxygen saturation 95% on room air.
Extremities: 1+ lower-extremity edema.
Renal: Renal allograft function stable. Creatinine improved to 1.25 from prior 1.4-1.5 range.
Echocardiogram: LVEF 50%, normal RV systolic function, dilated IVC with estimated RAP 15 mmHg, pulmonary artery pressure approximately 46 mmHg.
Assessment


Congestive heart failure/volume overload requiring ongoing diuretic therapy (ICD-10: I50.9)


Atrial fibrillation with recent rapid ventricular response, now in sinus rhythm on amiodarone (ICD-10: I48.91)


Long-term anticoagulant therapy with Eliquis (ICD-10: Z79.01)


Acute kidney injury, improved (ICD-10: N17.9)


Kidney transplant status (ICD-10: Z94.0)


Liver transplant status (ICD-10: Z94.4)


Essential hypertension (ICD-10: I10)


Obstructive sleep apnea (ICD-10: G47.33)


Plan


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to congestive heart failure management requiring continued diuresis, recent atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, anticoagulation management, and monitoring of cardiac and renal function in a patient with transplant history.


Continue diuretic therapy for congestive heart failure and volume management.


Continue oral amiodarone.


Continue Eliquis anticoagulation strategy as clinically appropriate.


Continue telemetry monitoring for recurrent atrial fibrillation or significant rhythm changes.


Monitor volume status, renal function, intake/output, and response to diuretic therapy.


Continue coordination with medicine team.


Continue UCLA follow-up for transplant-related care.


Arrange outpatient cardiology follow-up as appropriate after discharge.


Continue PT/OT and mobilization as tolerated.


Nursing Communication


Continue telemetry and cardiac medications as ordered.


Monitor for recurrent atrial fibrillation, significant bradycardia, hypotension, worsening dyspnea, increasing edema, or other clinical deterioration.


Monitor renal function, intake/output, and response to diuretic therapy.


Notify physician when patient's wife is present if feasible.

ROS STE - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


69-year-old man with predominantly right-sided heart failure, coronary artery disease, ventricular tachycardia, prior atrial fibrillation ablation, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic venous insufficiency with bilateral lower-extremity wounds.


History of MSSA bacteremia with prior infected ICD requiring extraction. A leadless pacemaker was subsequently placed, followed by subcutaneous ICD placement on 09/14/2026.


Reported ICD shock on 09/15/2026 was reviewed by device interrogation and documented as inappropriate therapy related to noise detection, possibly from an air bubble within the device pocket. ICD was subsequently turned off.


Known occlusive left subclavian vein DVT and superficial left basilic vein thrombosis.


Right-sided heart failure with prior echocardiographic findings of LVEF approximately 45%, dilated right ventricle, and estimated RV systolic pressure approximately 75 mmHg.


Ongoing management includes volume assessment, diuresis, anticoagulation decision-making, wound infection treatment, and skilled nursing facility planning.


SOAP Note
Subjective


Patient evaluated during inpatient cardiology follow-up.


Reports doing reasonably well from a cardiovascular standpoint.


Recent subcutaneous ICD placement and subsequent shock were reviewed.


Device interrogation reportedly demonstrated noise detection, possibly related to air within the device pocket, with the shock considered inappropriate rather than a confirmed ventricular arrhythmia.


ICD remains deactivated pending further discussion with electrophysiology regarding possible reactivation.


Patient and family expressed concern regarding the amount of physical therapy received during hospitalization.


Skilled nursing facility placement is being planned.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Alert and oriented, no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Predominantly right-sided heart failure. History of ventricular tachycardia. Recent subcutaneous ICD placement with documented inappropriate shock and subsequent deactivation.
Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally. Oxygen saturation 100% on room air.
Extremities: Chronic bilateral lower-extremity wounds with Unna boots. Known left upper-extremity venous thrombosis.
Neurologic: No focal findings documented.
Laboratory data reviewed. WBC 17.9 K/µL, hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL, hematocrit 26.6%, platelets 290 K/µL, sodium 133 mmol/L, potassium 4.8 mmol/L, BUN 61 mg/dL, creatinine 1.44 mg/dL, glucose 191 mg/dL.
Imaging reviewed:


Left upper-extremity venous duplex demonstrated occlusive thrombus within the left subclavian vein and superficial thrombosis of the left basilic vein.


Lower-extremity venous duplex without evidence of DVT; significant venous waveform pulsatility compatible with elevated right-sided pressures.


Assessment


Predominantly right-sided heart failure (ICD-10: I50.810)


Ventricular tachycardia with recent subcutaneous ICD placement and inappropriate device shock (ICD-10: I47.20, Z95.810)


Acute occlusive left subclavian deep venous thrombosis (ICD-10: I82.622)


Chronic kidney disease (ICD-10: N18.9)


Chronic bilateral lower-extremity wounds with venous insufficiency and Pseudomonas infection (ICD-10: T14.8XXA, I87.2)


Acute on chronic anemia (ICD-10: D64.9)


Coronary artery disease (ICD-10: I25.10)


History of atrial fibrillation status post ablation (ICD-10: Z98.890)


Leukocytosis (ICD-10: D72.829)


Hyponatremia (ICD-10: E87.1)


Type 2 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E11.9)


Essential hypertension (ICD-10: I10)


Plan


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to right-sided heart failure, recent ICD placement complicated by inappropriate shock requiring device management, confirmed venous thrombosis, chronic infected wounds requiring prolonged IV antibiotics, anemia, renal dysfunction, and disposition coordination.


Continue discussion with electrophysiology regarding ICD status and possible reactivation before discharge.


Continue volume assessment and diuretic management with bumetanide.


Monitor daily weights, intake/output, renal function, sodium, potassium, edema, and overall volume status.


Review anticoagulation plan for left subclavian DVT. Eliquis timing should be coordinated with bleeding risk assessment and treating team recommendations.


Continue wound care and bilateral Unna boot management.


Continue IV cefepime for Pseudomonas wound infection per infectious disease plan.


Continue monitoring hemoglobin given acute on chronic anemia and prior negative GI bleeding evaluation.


Continue renal function monitoring during diuretic therapy.


Continue telemetry monitoring.


Continue PT/OT and coordinate skilled nursing facility disposition planning.


Nursing Communication


Continue telemetry and heart failure monitoring.


Confirm final ICD plan with electrophysiology prior to discharge.


Monitor for recurrent palpitations, syncope, sustained ventricular arrhythmia, chest pain, hypotension, or worsening heart failure symptoms.


Monitor left upper extremity for worsening swelling, pain, discoloration, or neurovascular changes related to known DVT.


Eliquis remains held per current cardiology plan; do not resume without confirmation from the treating team.


Continue IV cefepime and bilateral lower-extremity wound care.


Continue PT/OT and assist with disposition planning.

ANT KRO - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features


95-year-old man with congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation on Xarelto, COPD, hypertension, biventricular ICD, and prior mitral and tricuspid valve repair.


Admitted with acute hypoxic respiratory failure in the setting of community-acquired pneumonia, COPD exacerbation, and possible acute decompensated heart failure.


Initial hypoxemia required supplemental oxygen, with improvement to lower oxygen requirement during hospitalization.


Ongoing volume management with diuresis and monitoring of hemodynamics, renal function, electrolytes, and urine output.


ECG demonstrates ventricular paced rhythm without acute ischemic changes.


Echocardiogram results and cardiac function remain under review.


SOAP Note
Subjective


Patient evaluated during inpatient cardiology follow-up.


Reports improvement in breathing but continues to have cough and congestion with light yellow sputum production.


Reports lower chest discomfort associated with coughing and deep inspiration.


Tolerating diet and denies abdominal complaints.


Family support and outpatient cardiology follow-up reviewed.


Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Pleasant and cooperative, sitting up in bed, conversational, no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1 and S2 present. Systolic ejection murmur noted. History of biventricular ICD.
Respiratory: Decreased air entry bilaterally with scattered rhonchi and bibasilar rales. No significant expiratory wheezing documented.
Abdomen: Soft, nontender, nondistended.
Extremities: Trace bilateral lower extremity edema. No cyanosis or clubbing.
Neurologic: Alert and oriented, nonfocal.
Laboratory data reviewed. WBC 11.1 K/µL, hemoglobin 10.3 g/dL, platelets 130 K/µL, sodium 133 mmol/L, potassium 4.3 mmol/L, BUN 21 mg/dL, creatinine 0.53 mg/dL, albumin 3.5 g/dL.
Imaging reviewed: Chest imaging with interstitial opacities consistent with possible pulmonary edema, atypical infection, and small right pleural effusion.
Assessment


Acute hypoxic respiratory failure (ICD-10: J96.01)


Community-acquired pneumonia (ICD-10: J18.9)


COPD with acute exacerbation (ICD-10: J44.1)


Congestive heart failure with possible volume overload (ICD-10: I50.9)


Atrial fibrillation (ICD-10: I48.91)


Presence of biventricular ICD (ICD-10: Z95.810)


Essential hypertension (ICD-10: I10)


Hypothyroidism (ICD-10: E03.9)


Chronic urinary retention with chronic indwelling Foley catheter (ICD-10: R33.9, Z97.8)


Chronic pain syndrome with chronic narcotic dependence (ICD-10: G89.4, F11.20)


Plan


High-complexity medical decision-making performed due to acute hypoxic respiratory failure with overlapping pneumonia, COPD exacerbation, and possible heart failure exacerbation in a patient with significant cardiac history including atrial fibrillation and biventricular ICD.


Continue ceftriaxone and azithromycin for pneumonia treatment.


Continue pulmonary therapy with Dulera, DuoNeb treatments, albuterol as needed, pulmonary hygiene, incentive spirometry, and CPAP as needed.


Continue diuresis with furosemide and monitor response.


Maintain strict intake and output, daily weights, renal function, electrolytes, and blood pressure monitoring.


Review echocardiogram results and images when available.


Continue metoprolol for rate control.


Continue Xarelto for anticoagulation unless contraindications develop.


Continue telemetry monitoring and monitor ICD status as clinically indicated.


Continue Foley catheter care and monitor urine output.


Continue chronic pain management regimen while minimizing additional narcotic use when possible.


Continue PT/OT and discharge planning when respiratory and volume status improve.


Nursing Communication


Continue telemetry monitoring.


Monitor respiratory status, oxygen requirement, intake/output, daily weights, renal function, and electrolytes.


Administer diuretics as ordered and monitor response.


Continue antibiotics, nebulizer therapy, and pulmonary hygiene.


Notify cardiology for worsening dyspnea, chest pain, arrhythmia, hypotension, or other clinical deterioration.


Continue Xarelto as ordered unless contraindications develop.


Continue Foley catheter care and monitor urine output.
